title: Starting on ukulele, banjo and guitar; lessons and joining Isaiah Morgan
summary: Born in Donaldsonville in 1910, taught piano rudiments by his mother, then ukulele; moves to New Orleans in 1925, takes banjo and guitar lessons from several teachers, then goes on the road with Isaiah Morgan and names his sidemen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: Well, I was born in Donisonville, Louisiana on December 12, 1910. And I started music at about six years old. Started on the piano, my mother started teaching me rudiments on the piano. But I didn't like the piano. And I put the piano down and I got a ukulele. And I started in the country on the ukulele. Then by 1925 I came to New Orleans. Then I played the ukulele on the shoeshine stands and around the streets of New Orleans for years. And then I got a banjo. And I started taking the banjo from lessons from Eddie Morgan and Professor Valmore Victor. And I put the, the guitar was getting popular way back there, and that was around the middle 30s. And I started taking lessons from a man by the name of Rainey Hall. Then he recommended me to Homer Eugene. Homer and I was taking lessons at the same time from Rainey Hall. And then when Rainey Hall left here, then I started taking lessons from Johnny Sincere. He was living back on Edinburgh Street. That's the last man that I took lessons from. Then I was about ready to try to play something. Then Isaiah Morgan took me. Then I went on the road with Isaiah Morgan. And the many people that he had in his band at the time was Thomas Jefferson on trumpet. He had Ernest Poirier on saxophone. He had a bass player by the name of Cleo. You ever heard him?
Yeah, but I never did know his right name. His full name. Did you know? And he had a, no I forgot, but I could get it. I'd love to know his right name. Everybody says he would.
